note: tmgmt_google_v3 adds ONE TMGMT translator plugin, id 'google_v3' (Drupal\tmgmt_google_v3\Plugin\tmgmt\Translator\GoogleV3Translator, UI GoogleV3TranslatorUi), sending jobs to the Google Cloud Translation v3 API. No settings page (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush; all config lives on a tmgmt_translator (provider) config entity using this plugin. Settings: location (default global), api_project (Google project id), google_credentials (managed JSON key in private://), glossary_mappings (per-langcode glossary id). LIVE translation needs a real Google service-account key which this environment does NOT have, so medium/hard cases are grounded ONLY in the provider config the agent can set without a key: creating the tmgmt_translator with plugin google_v3 and setting its location / api_project. Providers are namespaced tmgmtg_*. Extension point: PostTranslationEvent ('post_translation').

evals.prompt: How do I set up Google Cloud Translation v3 as a machine-translation provider in TMGMT using the tmgmt_google_v3 module? What do I create, and which settings must I supply?
evals.expected_output: Create a TMGMT Translator (translation provider) that uses the Google V3 plugin (id google_v3) and set its Location (default global), Project ID (api_project) and upload the Google service-account JSON credentials (stored in the private file system). There is no separate module settings page.

evals.prompt: The tmgmt_google_v3 translator asks me to upload a Google API credentials JSON file. Where is that file stored, and what filesystem must be enabled for it to work?
evals.expected_output: The credentials JSON key is uploaded as a managed file to the private filesystem (private://), so the private file system must be enabled. The file is marked permanent on save and only .json is allowed.

evals.prompt: In tmgmt_google_v3, how can I enforce consistent domain terminology per language, and how would a custom module post-process each string returned by Google before it is saved?
evals.expected_output: Use the translator's Glossary mappings (glossary_mappings) to map a Drupal language to a Google glossary id. To post-process output, subscribe to PostTranslationEvent (event name 'post_translation') and use getTranslatedText()/setTranslatedText().

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a TMGMT translation provider that uses the Google V3 plugin. Inspect the live provider configuration and report the Google Cloud Project ID (api_project) it is configured with.
evals.expected_output: The provider tmgmt.translator.tmgmtg_probe (plugin google_v3) has settings.api_project = 'tmgmtg-probe-project' (and location us-central1).

evals.prompt: A TMGMT translation provider labelled 'TMGMTG Probe Provider' exists on this site. Inspect the live configuration and report which translator plugin id it uses.
evals.expected_output: The provider tmgmt.translator.tmgmtg_probe uses translator plugin 'google_v3'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a TMGMT translation provider (Translator) with the machine name 'tmgmtg_task' that uses the Google V3 translator plugin (tmgmt_google_v3). Save it to the live site. (No real Google credentials are needed for this step.)
evals.expected_output: A tmgmt_translator config entity named tmgmtg_task exists with plugin 'google_v3' (tmgmt.translator.tmgmtg_task).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Google V3 TMGMT provider 'tmgmtg_cfg' with no Google Cloud Project ID configured. Set its Project ID (api_project) to your Google Cloud project (any non-empty value, e.g. 'my-gcp-project') and save the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: tmgmt.translator.tmgmtg_cfg (plugin google_v3) has a non-empty settings.api_project value.
